items.title: Gordon Lorraine — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was no particular kinship outside of the warmth of recording together... And Fats was one of them.

ctx.x: Then somebody that died so early, but you had a chance to meet and get to know him: Fats Navarro.

Oh, yeah, Fats. Well, you see, all these musicians were suddenly crowding into the Blue Note area. Because Alfred learned more and more, met more and more, got more and more involved, and all these great artists started arriving. Fats was a fabulous trumpet player. I mean, he was what his name is—Fats. He was adorable. I didn’t go into anything but musical experiences with these men. Some would come home and be friends with Alfred and me, and some were just artists who played for us. That was it. “We want your…
Do you feel his playing reflected who he was as a person? His soul? What was Fats like as a person?
